post.caption:
A photo is a count of photons per sensor well over a set time, and the three dials are aperture, shutter and sensitivity. Longer exposure means more light and more motion blur; more amplification means a usable frame full of noise. Which is why your phone does not take one photo. It takes a burst at different settings and merges them, keeping the sharp parts of one and the clean parts of another. The image you keep is a reconstruction that was never on the sensor.
